full_judgment: 7. As to the question whether a revision lies before the Sessions Judge under section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against an order passed by an Assistant Sessions Judge, the decision must be found in the answer to the question whether an Assistant Sessions Judges is an inferior criminal Court in relation to the Sessions Judge within the meaning of the aforesaid section. It is well settled that the term `inferior' does not carry with it any stigma or any suggestion that one Court is under the administrative orders of the superior Court. `Inferior' means one who is statutorily incompetent to hold or exercise equal power, it carries with it the idea of subordination which means `inferior in rank'. It is also well settled that the term 'inferior' must be interpreted to mean judicially inferior' i.e. a Court over which the Court proceeding under section 435 has appellate jurisdiction. Keeping their well-settled principles in view let us see whether an Assistant Sessions Judge can be said to be an inferior criminal Court in relation to the Sessions Judge. Undisputedly, the powers of the Sessions Judge are higher compared to that of the Assistant Sessions Judge which will be Clear from the provisions of section 31 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. An Assistant Sessions Judge has no power of reference and revision besides being vested with lesser powers, an Assistant Sessions Judge has been statutorily made subordinate to the Sessions Judge under section 17(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure ft is to be noted that there may be inferiority without subordination but there cannot be subordination without inferiority. While considering the question of inferiority it has been held in very many cases that a Court will be considered inferior to the Court to which appeal lies from the former. Section 408 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that an appeal from an order of conviction passed by an Assistant Sessions Judge shall lie to the Court of Sessions subject, however, to the proviso that in case of a sentence of imprisonment for a term exceeding 5 years or any sentence of transportation, the appeal shall lie to the High Court Division. It cannot be gainsaid that the Court of Sessions has been made a forum of appeal from conviction recorded by an Assistant Sessions Judge subject to certain limitation as to quantum of sentence.
